IMPLEMENT THIS EXACT APPROVED LESSON CONTENT:

SUBJECT:
Science

GRADE:
Grade 1

LESSON:
Lesson 1

TITLE:
Living & Nonliving Things 🌱

SUBTITLE:
Learn how to tell whether something is living or nonliving by looking for signs of life.

ESTIMATED TIME:
20–25 minutes

==================================================
LEARNING GOALS 🎯
==================================================

By the end of this lesson, the learner should be able to:

• Identify common living and nonliving things.
• Describe simple signs that show something is living.
• Explain that living things need resources such as water and energy.
• Recognize that living things grow and change.
• Use evidence to decide whether something is living or nonliving.

==================================================
OPENING — LOOK AROUND YOU 👀
==================================================

Look around you.

You might see a person, a plant, a pet, a chair, a pencil, a rock, or a toy.

Some of these are living things.
Others are nonliving things.

A dog is living. 🐕
A tree is living. 🌳
You are living. 🧒

A rock is nonliving. 🪨
A chair is nonliving. 🪑
A toy car is nonliving. 🚗

Sometimes the answer seems easy.

But what about a seed that is not moving?
What about a robot that can walk?
What about a wooden table that came from a tree?

To answer correctly, we need to look for signs of life.

==================================================
SECTION 1 — WHAT IS A LIVING THING? 🌱
==================================================

A living thing is something that carries out the processes of life.

People, animals, and plants are living things.

Living things have several important characteristics.

Living things:

💧 need resources such as water;
⚡ need energy;
🌱 grow and change;
👀 respond to things around them;
🐣 come from other living things of their kind.

We should not use only one clue.

Instead, we look for several signs of life together.

--------------------------------------------------
EXAMPLE: A PUPPY 🐶
--------------------------------------------------

Think about a puppy.

A puppy drinks water.

It eats food to get energy.

It grows bigger.

It reacts when it hears a sound.

It grows into an adult dog.

These are signs that the puppy is living.

==================================================
VISUAL 1 — LIVING OR NONLIVING?
==================================================

Create a bright, child-friendly comparison visual.

LEFT SIDE:
LIVING 🌱

🧒 Child
🐕 Dog
🐦 Bird
🌻 Flower

Labels around the group:

• Needs resources
• Grows
• Responds
• Has a life cycle

RIGHT SIDE:
NONLIVING 🧸

🪨 Rock
🪑 Chair
🚗 Toy car
✏️ Pencil

Label:

• Does not carry out life processes

Caption:

"Living things show signs of life. Nonliving things do not."

This visual should be lesson-specific, not the generic science orbital graphic.

==================================================
SECTION 2 — LIVING THINGS NEED RESOURCES 💧
==================================================

Living things need things from their surroundings in order to live.

Different living things have different needs, but many need water, air, energy, and a suitable place to live.

--------------------------------------------------
WATER 💧
--------------------------------------------------

People need water.

Animals need water.

Plants need water too.

Without enough water, living things may not stay healthy.

--------------------------------------------------
AIR 🌬️
--------------------------------------------------

People and many animals take oxygen from the air.

Plants also exchange gases with their surroundings.

Air is part of the environment that supports life.

--------------------------------------------------
ENERGY ⚡
--------------------------------------------------

Living things need energy.

Animals get energy from food. 🍎

Plants use light energy to make sugars they can use. ☀️🌱

For Grade 1, remember:

"Animals eat food. Plants use light to help make their food."

--------------------------------------------------
A PLACE TO LIVE 🏡
--------------------------------------------------

Living things need a place where their needs can be met.

A fish lives in water. 🐟

A bird may live in a nest. 🐦

A cactus can live in a dry place. 🌵

Different living things can live in different environments.

==================================================
VISUAL 2 — WHAT LIVING THINGS NEED
==================================================

Create a simple diagram with a plant and an animal in the center.

Around them place:

☀️ Light
💧 Water
🌬️ Air
🍎 Energy/Food
🏡 Suitable place to live

Use arrows pointing toward the living things.

Caption:

"Living things depend on resources from their environment."

==================================================
SECTION 3 — LIVING THINGS GROW AND CHANGE 🌱➡️🌻
==================================================

Living things do not stay exactly the same throughout their lives.

They grow and develop.

Think about a plant.

It may begin as a seed.

STEP 1:
A seed begins to germinate when conditions are suitable.

STEP 2:
A tiny root and shoot begin to grow.

STEP 3:
Leaves begin to develop.

STEP 4:
The plant becomes larger and more mature.

A living thing grows because of processes happening inside its body.

--------------------------------------------------
A PERSON GROWS TOO 🧒➡️🧑
--------------------------------------------------

A baby grows into a child.

A child grows into an adult.

The person remains the same living organism while growing and developing.

==================================================
VISUAL 3 — PLANT GROWTH SEQUENCE
==================================================

Create a horizontal illustrated sequence:

Seed
🌰

↓

Sprout
🌱

↓

Young Plant
🪴

↓

Mature Plant
🌻

Add arrows between each stage.

Caption:

"Living things grow and change during their lives."

==================================================
SECTION 4 — LIVING THINGS RESPOND 👂👀
==================================================

Living things can respond to changes around them.

This means they can react to their environment.

--------------------------------------------------
ANIMALS 🐕
--------------------------------------------------

A dog may turn its head when it hears its name.

A bird may fly away when it senses danger.

A person may pull a hand away from something very hot.

These are responses.

--------------------------------------------------
PLANTS 🌻
--------------------------------------------------

Plants respond too.

Their responses may be slower than an animal's movements.

For example, many plant shoots grow toward light.

Plants do not need to walk or run to be alive.

💡 REMEMBER:

"Not all living things move from place to place."

==================================================
SECTION 5 — MOVEMENT DOES NOT ALWAYS MEAN LIFE 🚗
==================================================

This is an important idea.

A car can move.

A fan can spin.

A robot can walk.

A cloud can move through the sky.

But these things are not living just because they move.

A toy car moves because a motor or a person makes it move.

A real dog moves because it is a living organism.

So this rule is wrong:

❌ "If it moves, it is alive."

A better rule is:

✅ "Look for several signs of life."

==================================================
WORKED EXAMPLE — IS A TOY ROBOT ALIVE? 🤖
==================================================

A toy robot can walk and make sounds.

Does that make it alive?

Let's check.

STEP 1:
Does the robot grow through biological growth?

No.

STEP 2:
Does the robot need food and water because it is alive?

No.

STEP 3:
Does it carry out life processes by itself?

No.

STEP 4:
Why does it move?

Its machine parts, battery, or motor make it move.

CONCLUSION:

The robot is nonliving.

⭐ Movement alone does not prove that something is alive.

==================================================
SECTION 6 — SOME LIVING THINGS LOOK STILL 🌰
==================================================

Something does not have to be moving all the time to be alive.

Think about a sleeping cat. 🐈💤

The cat may look very still.

But it is still breathing and using energy.

It is still alive.

Now think about a seed. 🌰

A seed may look dry and still.

But under suitable conditions, it can germinate and grow into a plant.

So this rule is also wrong:

❌ "If it is not moving, it is not alive."

==================================================
SECTION 7 — WHAT IS NONLIVING? 🪨
==================================================

A nonliving thing does not carry out the processes of life.

Examples include:

🪨 rocks
💧 water
🌬️ air
🪑 chairs
✏️ pencils
🧸 toys
🥤 cups
🚲 bicycles

Nonliving things can still change.

Ice can melt. 🧊➡️💧

A rock can break.

Metal can rust.

A balloon can get bigger when air is blown into it. 🎈

But these changes are not biological growth.

==================================================
SECTION 8 — THINGS THAT WERE ONCE LIVING 🌳➡️🪑
==================================================

Some nonliving things are made from materials that once came from living things.

Think about wood.

A tree is living. 🌳

A wooden table is not living. 🪑

The wood came from a living tree, but the table does not carry out life processes.

Paper is another example.

Paper can be made from plant material.

A sheet of paper is nonliving now. 📄

For this lesson, remember:

LIVING:
alive now

ONCE LIVING:
came from something that was alive

NEVER LIVING:
was never an organism

Both once-living and never-living objects are nonliving now.

==================================================
GUIDED EXAMPLE — IS A TREE LIVING? 🌳
==================================================

Let's investigate.

QUESTION 1:
Does a tree need resources?

Yes. ✅

It needs water, gases from the air, light, and nutrients.

QUESTION 2:
Does a tree grow?

Yes. ✅

A young tree can grow taller and develop more branches.

QUESTION 3:
Does it respond to its surroundings?

Yes. ✅

Plants respond to environmental conditions such as light.

QUESTION 4:
Does it have a life cycle?

Yes. ✅

New plants can develop from seeds or through other reproductive processes.

CONCLUSION:

🌳 A tree is a living thing.

==================================================
ACTIVITY — SORT THE OBJECTS 🧠
==================================================

Look at these objects:

🐈 Cat
🌻 Sunflower
🪨 Rock
🚲 Bicycle
🐟 Fish
🧸 Teddy bear

Sort them.

LIVING 🌱

🐈 Cat
🌻 Sunflower
🐟 Fish

NONLIVING 📦

🪨 Rock
🚲 Bicycle
🧸 Teddy bear

Now ask:

"What evidence helped you decide?"

A strong answer should mention signs of life such as:

• growth;
• needing resources;
• responding to surroundings;
• having a life cycle.

Do not use only:

"It moves."

==================================================
COMMON MISTAKES ⚠️
==================================================

MISTAKE 1:

"If something moves, it must be living."

❌ Not true.

Cars, fans, and robots can move but are nonliving.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 2:

"Plants are not living because they cannot walk."

❌ Not true.

Plants grow, use resources, respond to their surroundings, and have life cycles.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 3:

"If something gets bigger, it must be growing."

❌ Not always.

A balloon gets bigger when air is added.

That is not biological growth.

--------------------------------------------------

MISTAKE 4:

"If something is still, it is nonliving."

❌ Not true.

A sleeping animal is still alive.

A seed may also be alive even when it looks inactive.

==================================================
QUICK CHECK 🧠
==================================================

Think about each item before revealing the answer.

1. DOG 🐕
Living or nonliving?

Answer:
Living

Why?
It grows, needs resources, responds, and has a life cycle.

--------------------------------------------------

2. ROCK 🪨
Living or nonliving?

Answer:
Nonliving

Why?
It does not carry out life processes.

--------------------------------------------------

3. PLANT 🌱
Living or nonliving?

Answer:
Living

Why?
It grows, needs resources, and responds to its environment.

--------------------------------------------------

4. TOY CAR 🚗
Living or nonliving?

Answer:
Nonliving

Why?
Movement from a motor does not make it alive.

==================================================
KEY CONCEPT ⭐
==================================================

TITLE:

Living things show signs of life.

BODY:

Living things need resources, grow and develop, respond to their surroundings, and have life cycles.

Do not decide whether something is living by using only one clue.

Look for several signs of life together.

==================================================
FINAL RECAP 🌟
==================================================

Before leaving the lesson, remember:

🌱 Plants and animals are living things.

💧 Living things need resources.

📈 Living things grow and change.

👀 Living things respond to their surroundings.

🚗 Something can move and still be nonliving.

💤 Something can look still and still be alive.

🧠 Use several clues before deciding.
